title: CEO Interview with Vincent Cobée of ITEN
gist: ITEN, a French deep-tech company near Lyon, makes solid-state ceramic batteries for electronics rather than EVs. Its full-scale line became operational at the end of 2025, and its Powency high-power micro-batteries have been in mass production since mid-2025 with three references in volume. The higher-energy Flowency platform targets wearables and MedTech from 2028; CEO Vincent Cobée (ex-Citroën CEO) pitches PCB solderability, no thermal runaway and energy-harvesting pairing as the edge over supercapacitors, coin cells and Li-ion/LiPo.

themes.theme: ITEN funding, manufacturing scale and IP

insights.claim: French solid-state ceramic battery maker ITEN, founded at the end of 2011, has raised more than €110 million, including an €80 million round in 2022. It moved from a 2018 pilot line to a full-scale manufacturing line that became fully operational at the end of 2025.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: This is a modestly capitalized European solid-state battery maker that has just reached industrial scale, so it is a candidate for a later-stage raise, a strategic partnership or an acquisition by a component maker.
insights.quote: Our full-scale manufacturing line became fully operational at the end of 2025.

insights.claim: ITEN operates as an integrated device manufacturer, controlling materials, cell design, packaging, testing and production. It holds 48 patent families covering solid-state energy storage and its manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Owning the full value chain and a sizable patent estate raises barriers to entry and makes the company more valuable as an acquisition target in micro solid-state storage.

insights.claim: ITEN deliberately targets the electronics industry (IoT, smart cards, wearables, healthcare) rather than mobility, a notable choice given CEO Vincent Cobée's background as Citroën CEO and a Stellantis executive.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Solid-state batteries are reaching commercial volume first in small electronics, not EVs, so this niche is where to watch for early revenue proof points.
insights.quote: ITEN’s focus is the electronics industry rather than mobility.
insights.locator: ITEN’s focus is the electronics industry

insights.claim: ITEN's Powency family offers high power density in low capacities (up to a few tens of mAh) and has been in mass production since mid-2025, with three product references in volume production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Solid-state batteries are now commercially shipping in micro form factors, which de-risks the technology claim even though volumes are likely still small.
insights.locator: The company currently has two product families

insights.claim: ITEN plans to launch higher-capacity and higher-voltage Powency batteries in 2027. Its Flowency platform, which targets a few tens of mAh up to a few Ah with high energy density and fast recharge, aims to deliver a solid-state breakthrough for wearables and MedTech from 2028.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Use the 2027 and 2028 dates to track whether ITEN can move from tiny burst-power cells into the larger, higher-value wearable battery market.
insights.quote: The goal is to create a breakthrough in solid-state technologies for wearables and MedTech from 2028 onwards.
insights.locator: ITEN is continuing to expand the Powency

insights.claim: ITEN is developing manufacturing technology for custom-shaped batteries aimed at AI wearable devices, which could be integrated into the product's material or case. It is also building post-processing for System-in-Package (SiP) and embedded-die integration.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Battery form factor is becoming a design lever for AI wearables, which makes custom solid-state cells a possible enabler for that device category.
insights.locator: Another area of development is new manufacturing technology

themes.theme: Differentiation vs supercapacitors, coin cells and Li-ion

insights.claim: ITEN says competition from other solid-state battery suppliers is limited in electronics. Its real competitors are supercapacitors (many suppliers), primary coin cells and conventional Li-ion and LiPo battery makers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: In micro-power, solid-state cells win by displacing supercapacitors and coin cells, not by beating rival solid-state makers.

insights.claim: Powency cells can be soldered directly onto PCBs. ITEN says this can cut manufacturing cost compared with supercapacitors, which are placed on boards by hand, and the cells take up far less area or volume than bulky supercapacitors.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Lower assembly cost through automated, SMT-style placement is the concrete adoption driver to check in customer design wins.

insights.claim: ITEN's ceramic batteries contain no liquid electrolyte or organic components, which avoids swelling and thermal runaway. Powency devices are classed as electronic passive devices for air transport and can be recycled like passive components.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Simpler shipping and recycling rules remove logistics friction that weighs on lithium cells, which matters for IoT shipped in high volume.
insights.quote: Our batteries contain no liquid electrolyte or organic components, avoiding swelling and thermal runaway mechanisms.
insights.locator: Safety is also an important differentiator

insights.claim: ITEN's batteries can withstand high-temperature post-processing, so packaged or unpackaged cells can be co-integrated into a wide range of materials and mechatronic systems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Tolerance of high-temperature processing is a key enabler for embedding storage in packages and structures, which liquid-electrolyte cells cannot do.

themes.theme: IoT energy harvesting and MedTech use cases

insights.claim: ITEN argues that pairing rechargeable solid-state batteries with energy harvesting (wireless RF, solar, thermoelectric generators) can replace the primary batteries that long-lived IoT devices must frequently swap, addressing maintenance and recycling burdens.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Battery-free or maintenance-free Ambient IoT is the demand driver for rechargeable micro-storage, so watch Ambient IoT adoption as a leading indicator.
insights.locator: For IoT customers, one of the key concerns

insights.claim: ITEN and XPANCEO built a proof of concept that puts an ITEN solid-state energy storage device inside a smart contact lens. The cell has to fit an ultra-thin, curved device on the eye while powering wireless connectivity and AR functions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: This is an extreme miniaturization showcase that signals possible use in next-gen AR form factors, though it is only a proof of concept.

insights.claim: Through SOLIMED, a project within the European IPCEI Tech4Cure initiative, ITEN is developing batteries for Class III implantable medical devices. The first target is implantable cardiac pumps, and the work also covers wireless recharging and biocompatible encapsulation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: EU state-aid backing through IPCEI gives non-dilutive support, and Class III implants are a high-margin market that is slow to qualify for.
insights.locator: We are also addressing these challenges

insights.claim: ITEN works with customers through technical scoping and full custom battery development with dedicated teams. It also co-designs electronic boards to validate power-management architectures around Powency and provides reference designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A high-touch, custom-heavy model suggests long design-in cycles and lumpy early revenue, but sticky customers once they design ITEN in.
insights.locator: Customer engagement starts with technical discussions
